pages.text:
Burning in oxygen instead of air makes a hotter, more efficient flame. The Firebox and the Fuel Burner both take oxygen.
# Setting up
- With the Wrench in Port mode (or in the Sides tab), set a face to Oxygen.
- Pipe oxygen in with a Pressurized Conduit, from an Electrolyzer, an Air Separator or a Pressurized Cylinder. The machine keeps a small oxygen tank (2,000 mB).
# What it does
While it has oxygen, a burning machine:
- burns 300°C hotter, up to 1,600°C;
- makes 25% more heat from each fuel;
- uses 0.25 mB of oxygen per tick.
Without oxygen it works exactly as before. The flame in the GUI turns blue-white and the status reads Oxy-fuel. The Heat tab shows how much oxygen is left.

# Why bother
- A Firebox on oxy-fuel reaches 1,400°C: hot enough for Superheated Steam, which needs 900°C, with room to spare.
- A Fuel Burner on hydrogen and oxygen hits the 1,600°C cap.
- An Electrolyzer makes 1 mB of oxygen with every 2 mB of hydrogen, so a hydrogen burner can feed on its own oxygen.
